title: Like dissolves like
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:32:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the general like-dissolves-like principle: the shapes card covers molecular polarity only, and the hydrocarbons card is narrower, covering non-polar hydrocarbons and dispersion forces, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Like dissolves like
card: A polar molecule has an uneven spread of charge, so one end is slightly positive and the other slightly negative. A non-polar molecule has an even spread of charge.
Polar solutes tend to dissolve in polar solvents, such as water. Ionic compounds like sodium chloride also dissolve in water, as the water molecules attract the ions.
Non-polar solutes tend to dissolve in non-polar solvents, such as hexane. Oils and fats dissolve in hexane.
A polar solute and a non-polar solvent usually do not mix. The attractions between the particles of each substance are stronger than the attractions between the two different substances.
draft.remember: Match the solute to the solvent: polar with polar, non-polar with non-polar.

a.q: Which solvent is best for dissolving a non-polar wax?
opts: Hexane, a non-polar liquid
Water, a polar liquid
Salt water, a solution of ions
Ethanol, a polar liquid
a.why: Wax is non-polar, so it dissolves best in a non-polar solvent such as hexane. Water is the tempting choice because it is the most common solvent, but it is polar and does not dissolve non-polar wax well.
a.clue: Match the polarity of the solvent to the wax.

b.q: Priya spills cooking oil on a bench. Water barely cleans it, but hexane removes it easily. What explains this?
opts: Oil is non-polar, so it mixes with non-polar hexane
Oil is polar, so it mixes with non-polar hexane
Oil is non-polar, so it mixes with polar water
Oil is ionic, so it mixes with non-polar hexane
b.why: Oil is non-polar, so it dissolves in non-polar hexane but not in polar water. The option saying oil is non-polar and mixes with water is tempting, but it reverses the rule and does not fit what Priya saw.
b.clue: Decide whether oil is polar, then pick the matching solvent.

b.best: Oil is non-polar, so it mixes with non-polar hexane

problems.detail: 'Ionic compounds like sodium chloride also dissolve in water' can be read as saying all ionic compounds dissolve in water. Many, such as silver chloride and calcium carbonate, are insoluble. A word like 'many' would avoid teaching a false generalisation.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, with one clearly correct answer each. The only problem is that the card's sentence on ionic compounds could suggest that all of them dissolve in water.
